title.english: Giving and Receiving: あげる, くれる, もらう
title.japanese: あげる・くれる・もらう

body:
## Three Verbs Where English Has Two

English gets by with "give" and "receive." Japanese splits "give" in two according to the direction of the gift relative to the speaker, and adds a "receive" verb whose subject is the person on the receiving end. Choosing among ⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧, ⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧, and ⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧ is not optional: the wrong verb sounds as odd as saying "I gave a present from her" in English.

| Verb | Subject | Direction |
|------|---------|-----------|
| ⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧ | the giver | from me (or my side) to someone else; or from one outsider to another |
| ⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ | the giver | from someone else to me (or my side) |
| ⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧ | the receiver | receiving, from anyone |

## ⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧: Giving Outward

⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧ is used when you (or someone on your side) give to someone else, and when you describe giving between two other people.

- ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{妹|いもうと}→妹：00573_imouto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{本|ほん}→本：00111_hon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦あげた→あげる：00546_ageru⟧。 — I gave my younger sister a book.
- ⟦{田中|たなか}→田中：09528_tanaka⟧さん⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{山田|やまだ}→山田：09529_yamada⟧さん⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{土産|みやげ}→お土産：01353_omiyage⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦あげました→あげる：00546_ageru⟧。 — Tanaka gave Yamada a souvenir.

Two neighbors of ⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧ are worth knowing. ⟦やる→やる：02980_yaru⟧ is the plain, slightly rough verb for giving to animals, plants, and (in casual masculine speech) children or juniors: ⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{餌|えさ}→餌：01886_esa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦やる→やる：02980_yaru⟧ (to feed the dog), ⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦やる→やる：02980_yaru⟧ (to water the flowers). ⟦{差|さ}し{上|あ}げる→差し上げる：01597_sashiageru⟧ is the humble equivalent used toward a superior: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{差|さ}し{上|あ}げた→差し上げる：01597_sashiageru⟧ (I gave my teacher a letter). Even so, describing your own gift to a superior with a giving verb can sound as if you were doing them a favor, so people often avoid the verb and say お⟦{持|も}ち→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧ or ⟦{受|う}け{取|と}って→受け取る：01883_uketoru⟧⟦いただけます→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧ instead.

## ⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧: Giving Toward Me

⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ is used when someone else gives to you, or to a person you speak for: your family, your company, your team. The giver is the subject.

- ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧（⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧）⟦チョコレート→チョコレート：05183_chokoreeto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。 — A friend gave me chocolate.
- ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{弟|おとうと}→弟：00572_otouto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{辞書|じしょ}→辞書：04707_jisho⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦くださった→くださる：01305_kudasaru⟧。 — The teacher gave my little brother a dictionary.

Because ⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ already points at the speaker, ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ is usually left out. In the second sentence the receiver is the speaker's brother, so the giving still comes toward "my side," and the teacher's higher status turns ⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ into its respectful form ⟦くださる→くださる：01305_kudasaru⟧.

## ⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧: Receiving

⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧ takes the receiver as its subject and marks the giver with ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ or ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧. ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧ is required when the giver is an organization or a place rather than a person.

- ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{年玉|としだま}→お年玉：08452_otoshidama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。 — I got New Year's money from my grandmother.
- ⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{記念品|きねんひん}→記念品：03049_kinenhin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらいました→もらう：00520_morau⟧。 — I received a commemorative gift from the company.
- ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{推薦状|すいせんじょう}→推薦状：15195_suisenjou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦いただいた→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧。 — I received a letter of recommendation from my teacher.

⟦いただく→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧ is the humble form of ⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧, and the same verb is used for receiving food and drink — which is where the mealtime ⟦いただきます→いただきます：00946_itadakimasu⟧ comes from.

## Who Counts as "Me"?

The line between ⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧ and ⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ is not really about "I" and "you" but about the speaker's own circle and everyone outside it. Your family, your company, and your close group belong to your side when you speak to outsiders, so a neighbor who gives sweets to your daughter ⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ — お⟦{隣|となり}→隣：01003_tonari⟧さん⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{娘|むすめ}→娘：02263_musume⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧. When both giver and receiver are on your side, use ⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧ to describe the event from outside (⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{弟|おとうと}→弟：00572_otouto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{金|かね}→お金：00611_okane⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦あげた→あげる：00546_ageru⟧), and ⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ only when the receiver is you or someone you speak for.

## Doing Favors: 〜て⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧, 〜て⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧, 〜て⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧

The same three verbs attach to the te-form of any verb to show that an action was done as a favor, and in which direction.

- ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{宿題|しゅくだい}→宿題：00812_shukudai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{手伝|てつだ}って→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧⟦あげた→あげる：00546_ageru⟧。 — I helped my friend with homework (as a favor).
- ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{宿題|しゅくだい}→宿題：00812_shukudai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{手伝|てつだ}って→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。 — My friend helped me with my homework.
- ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{宿題|しゅくだい}→宿題：00812_shukudai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{手伝|てつだ}って→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。 — I had my friend help me with my homework.

〜て⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ and 〜て⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧ carry a note of gratitude, and leaving them out makes a sentence sound flat or even cold: ⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{弁当|べんとう}→弁当：01014_bentou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧ simply reports the fact, while ⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{弁当|べんとう}→弁当：01014_bentou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}って→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ acknowledges the kindness. The polite counterparts follow the pattern of the plain verbs: 〜て⟦くださる→くださる：01305_kudasaru⟧ for someone above you doing you a favor (⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{説明|せつめい}して→説明する：05639_setsumeisuru⟧⟦くださいました→くださる：01305_kudasaru⟧), and 〜て⟦いただく→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧ for receiving one (⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{説明|せつめい}して→説明する：05639_setsumeisuru⟧⟦いただいた→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧).

〜て⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧, on the other hand, calls attention to your own kindness. It is fine among friends and family, but toward a superior it sounds patronizing. To offer help to your boss, say ⟦お{手伝|てつだ}い→お手伝い：07775_otetsudai⟧⟦します→する：00392_suru⟧ or ⟦{手伝|てつだ}いましょう→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧, not ⟦{手伝|てつだ}って→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧.

## Asking for a Favor

Requests are built on the same verbs, and each step adds politeness:

- ⟦{手伝|てつだ}って→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧？ / ⟦{手伝|てつだ}って→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧⟦くれない→くれる：00724_kureru⟧？ — Can you help me? (casual)
- ⟦{手伝|てつだ}って→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧⟦くれません→くれる：00724_kureru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧ / ⟦{手伝|てつだ}って→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧⟦もらえます→もらう：00520_morau⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧ — Could you help me? (polite)
- ⟦{手伝|てつだ}って→手伝う：00898_tetsudau⟧⟦いただけません→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧ — Would you be able to help me? (very polite)

⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧ is the imperative form of ⟦くださる→くださる：01305_kudasaru⟧, which is why 〜て⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧ means "please do" and ⟦お{茶|ちゃ}→お茶：00576_ocha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧ means "please give me tea"; its casual cousin ⟦ちょうだい→ちょうだい：03435_choudai⟧ (⟦{見|み}せて→見せる：01988_miseru⟧⟦ちょうだい→ちょうだい：03435_choudai⟧, ⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧⟦ちょうだい→ちょうだい：03435_choudai⟧) is common in family speech.

## Common Mistakes

1. **Using ⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧ for a gift to yourself.** ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{本|ほん}→本：00111_hon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦あげました→あげる：00546_ageru⟧ is wrong; the gift comes toward you, so it is ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{本|ほん}→本：00111_hon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦くださいました→くださる：01305_kudasaru⟧.
2. **Making the giver the subject of ⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧.** The receiver is the subject: ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧, never ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧.
3. **Offering 〜て⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧ to a superior.** Use humble お〜⟦します→する：00392_suru⟧ instead.
4. **Dropping the favor verb.** If someone did something for you, add 〜て⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ or 〜て⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧; without it, the sentence does not express that you benefited.

## Tips for Learners

1. **Think in arrows.** Ask where the thing is going: away from me (⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧), toward me (⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧), or into my hands (⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧).
2. **Learn the polite trio as a set.** ⟦{差|さ}し{上|あ}げる→差し上げる：01597_sashiageru⟧, ⟦くださる→くださる：01305_kudasaru⟧, and ⟦いただく→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧ are the same three arrows one level up.
3. **Reach for 〜て⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧ and 〜て⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧ often.** Native speakers use them whenever a favor was involved; learners use them far too rarely.
4. **Mark organizations with から.** ⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧, ⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧, ⟦{市|し}→市：01599_shi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧ — ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ is for people.
5. **Read the related entries.** The entries for the giving verbs, and for ⟦{恩|おん}→恩：02550_on⟧ (a debt of gratitude) and ⟦{身内|みうち}→身内：14300_miuchi⟧ (one's own circle), give more of the social background.
